title: Rebuilding Small Businesses After Disasters Act
official_summary:
Rebuilding Small Businesses After Disasters Act

This bill makes permanent the increased threshold for the minimum major-disaster loan amount for which the Small Business Administration may require collateral.

summary.headline: Makes permanent a higher dollar threshold above which the Small Business Administration may require collateral on disaster loans to small businesses.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes a rule about disaster loans from the Small Business Administration. Under the rule, the agency can ask a borrower to pledge collateral only when a loan is above a set dollar amount. This law makes a higher version of that amount permanent instead of temporary. The summary provided does not give the specific dollar figures.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses that borrow from the Small Business Administration after a major disaster
who_it_affects.how: Smaller disaster loans are less likely to require pledged collateral under the higher threshold.

who_it_affects.group: Homeowners and nonprofits that apply for SBA disaster loans
who_it_affects.how: The same collateral threshold applies to their disaster loans, so they may be affected in the same way.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on November 22, 2019, the higher threshold became permanent.
